answer: Proof of Stake protocols resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as a ledge of collateral. If an attacker attempts to wander across the network by spinning up thousands of illicit identities, they risk slashing, as the cost of acquiring sufficient stake becomes prohibitively expensive. Like a zephyr moving against a fortified wall, fake identities fail to penetrate the consensus, as influence is strictly tied to economic risk rather than the mere volume of nodes.
